Natalie — thanks for the clear redline. I pulled in Karthik (legal) and Vanessa (ops) to make sure we reconcile contract language with operational constraints.

High-level responses:
- Pen-test window: Redwood can agree to a 30-day notice for production-impacting tests and will scope by environment. For staging-only tests we can accommodate a 14-day notice in most cases. We will enumerate systems in-scope in an appendix (protected link) and keep production carveouts where third-party infra providers require longer coordination.
- Evidence cadence: Redwood provides SOC 2 reports on an annual cadence to customers (or via secure portal for authorized recipients). For operational artifacts we propose quarterly snapshots for top-level controls and ad-hoc access for scoped requests under an approved evidence request workflow (we'll include SLAs for evidence turnaround).

Action items I’m proposing:
1) Attach a short "Assurance playbook" (redwood_soc2-summary.pdf) with the order form that documents notice windows, evidence cadence, who to contact, and the pen-test gating checklist.
2) Karthik to propose redline language for the pen-test clause and an appendix template.
3) Vanessa to confirm feasibility of the 14/30 day split and note any operational exceptions.

Can we aim to have a reconciled draft by end of week? If that's tight for you, suggest a short call Thursday 10–10:30am PT.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Order form — SOC 2 / pen-test language questions

Soojin / Vanessa / Natalie — I reviewed HealthCo's redline and drafted suggested contract language (see summary below). I focused on three items: scope clarity, notice SLAs, and evidence access controls. High-level:

A) Pen-test clause (proposed):
"Customer may conduct security testing of Redwood systems with prior written notice. For tests targeting Production, Customer shall provide at least thirty (30) calendar days' notice and shall only conduct tests within mutually agreed time windows. For tests limited to Staging or Non-Production environments, Customer shall provide at least fourteen (14) calendar days' notice. Redwood reserves the right to deny or reschedule tests that materially impact platform availability or violate third-party provider terms. Redwood will provide a non-exhaustive appendix listing typical in-scope components for Production and Staging; final scope to be agreed per-test."

B) Evidence cadence (proposed):
"Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II reports annually upon execution of an NDA and access request. Operational artifacts (configuration snapshots, audit logs, TLS cert inventories) will be provided on a quarterly snapshot basis for controls identified in the Security Exhibit; ad-hoc requests for additional artifacts will be evaluated and fulfilled under a documented evidence request workflow with a target 10 business day turnaround for routine requests and a mutually-agreed schedule for complex requests."

C) Operational carveouts: include a short list of items that require vendor/infra provider coordination (e.g., managed DB hosts, cloud provider-managed services) which may extend remediation/response timelines.

I attached a small redline file (orderform-redlines_v3.docx) with inline edits to HealthCo's document and a proposed appendix template. If the language above is acceptable conceptually, we can bake it into the order form and I’ll track any remaining open terms.

—Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: Order form — SOC 2 / pen-test language questions

Natalie — quick operational confirmation from my side: the 14/30 split is implementable with the following notes:

- Staging (14 days): we can support the majority of vendor-led tests in staging with standard snapshot and rollback playbooks. Exceptions include customers requesting elevated network access or long-running load tests — those will need case-by-case scheduling.
- Production (30 days): we require a pre-test runbook submission 10 business days before the test window to validate scope and rollback steps. Any test that requests elevated access to managed third-party services will require additional coordination and may shift the date.
- Evidence delivery: quarterly snapshots are fine for the control buckets we discussed. For ad-hoc requests that require logs older than 90 days or cross-region exports, we'll need to agree on export scope and may apply export labor (we'll include an SOW appendix option).

Next steps I recommend: 1) Karthik to incorporate the proposed language into the order form; 2) Soojin to attach the Assurance playbook to the order form package; 3) Natalie to confirm whether HealthCo is comfortable with the pre-test runbook and potential SOW carveouts.

If that works, I can open an internal ops ticket to enumerate in-scope components and share the appendix draft by EOD Monday.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
